title: Certify the exact forward Gaussian rounding threshold through radius 24 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Finite certificate for injective error-one rounding of the four-coordinate Hadamard/Gaussian pair. The verifier constructs and checks an exact integral orbit flow that saturates all 1,638,241 inputs in the radius-24 ball at forward norm slack `sqrt(78)-sqrt(73)`.

Combined with the radius-nine lower bound in #7571 at `3c7c3e8000f592fd9adecb44008ff6d5ae5d453d`, this gives the exact finite optimum at every real radius from 9 through 24. The new contribution is attainment through radius 24, including the larger balls left open in #7571. This settles the advance claim's bounded question without raising the global lower bound. [Claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19693299) · [Finding](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19693342)

## Evidence

Normal and optimized CPython 3.12.15 checks passed on arm64 Darwin in 1.81 and 1.65 seconds locally. Both print `PASS_GAUSSIAN_OUTWARD_RADIUS24` with 11,383 input orbits, 11,661 eligible output orbits and 21,458 positive orbit flows. The verification checks every used edge and both orbit capacities, and counts the input ball by a separate integer slice sum. The written lift uses biregularity and Hall's theorem. Both registered commands, metadata and source pins, and the five-file committed-byte and source-history checks passed.

Run from the repository root. Any CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the local path.

```sh
python312=/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12
"$python312" -I -W error -B research/gaussian-outward-radius24/verify.py
"$python312" -I -O -W error -B research/gaussian-outward-radius24/verify.py
"$python312" -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-outward-radius24
"$python312" -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/gaussian-outward-radius24 --check-source-history
```

## Limitations

The exact optimum uses #7571's lower bound as a cited premise. The new executable covers the radius-24 upper bound. Predecessor verifiers and the selected cold replay were unrun. All-lattice attainment, extra algebraic identities, physical costs and selected caller admission remain open. No new κ or assumption discharge. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

Credit CubeJerry for the finite Hall lower bound, orbit-flow method and larger-radius question, aliromman for the Gaussian pair in #6509, ywz65 for #2589's finite-ball boundary and petalas for #6619's zero-slack obstruction.

## Open next questions

- Can a radius-independent Hall argument give an all-lattice injection at the same threshold? Start by studying cuts that meet many distinct squared radii.
- Does the optimum survive the additional requirements of a specific Gaussian caller? Restrict the candidate edges to one named caller's exact-sum or phase identities before checking Hall cuts.

## Related open work

- #7571 proves the radius-nine lower bound used here. The radius-24 certificate extends its finite attainment result.
- #7569 constructs a global bijection under a bilateral radial-slack bound. This package certifies forward slack on finite balls.
- #7570 requires exact Gaussian sums and a prescribed square identity. This package's graph allows all error-one candidates.
- #7572 studies outward slack in affine-period and conserved-center families. This package's finite injection has no such requirement.
- #7652 studies the same forward quantity with exact sum imposed in a fixed fiber. The radius-24 graph allows all error-one outputs.

All three hosted checks passed at `4bcd4ecd13647798baa7ee6b95dd5e48ef1319ed`. The run covered planning, the historical replay-gap package, and the radius-24 Gaussian rounding package. [CI run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44199677817)
